tier_reason: Independent third-party shootout (r-lyeh Scriptorium) with public harness (bench.cc, run.bat, tests/fib.p, pawn/make.bat) whose table rows 6 and 8 show pawn-asm 0.384 s and pawn 0.719 s against PUC Lua 1.341 s; not A because the CPU is given only as 'AMD A10 3.8 GHz' (no model) and Lua's build flags are not stated.

corrections.workload: Scriptorium: recursive Fibonacci fib(34), whole-process wall time per run (bench.cc times system() calls, averaged over 5 runs, table keeps the best run), seconds, lower is better; 50 scripting-language implementations.
corrections.claimed_speedup: pawn-asm 0.384 s (page shows 'x03.4') and pawn 0.719 s ('x01.8') vs Lua 1.341 s (about 3.5x and 1.9x, derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: MSVC, VS2015 RC if possible, VS2013 elsewhere (per page); Pawn AMX built with cl /Ox /Oy /MT /DNDEBUG (pawn/make.bat), pawn-asm adds the AMX_ASM assembler core amxexec.asm assembled with 32-bit ml /coff; script compiled with pawncc -d0 -O3 (run.bat); Lua build flags not stated.
corrections.caveats: Single micro-benchmark (recursive fib(34)) from 2015-2016 on Windows 7, 'take it with a grain of salt'; times are whole-process wall time including startup. The 3.4x row is pawn-asm, the hand-written x86-32 assembler core (built with 32-bit ml); the portable C core is only 1.8x faster than PUC Lua, and LuaJIT (0.111 s) and even LuaJIT -joff (0.521 s) beat both Pawn rows. Pawn is a typeless 32-bit-cell language compiled ahead of time to bytecode, against dynamically typed Lua. A pawn-jit.exe was built but has no row (amxjitr.err in the folder). Pawn version used is not stated. The GitHub repo is archived (2025-09-26) and its README says the project moved to Codeberg (codeberg.org was blocked here, so activity there is unchecked). Licence is Apache-2.0 plus a static-linking exception; documentation is CC BY-SA 3.0.

notes: Numbers match Scriptorium rows exactly; tier B kept as independent shootout. Shortcomings: one recursive-fib test, main 3.4x figure needs the 32-bit x86 asm core (C core 1.8x), LuaJIT faster, GitHub repo archived (moved to Codeberg, unchecked).

tier_reason: Independent third-party shootout (r-lyeh Scriptorium) with public harness (bench.cc, run.bat, tests/fib.t) whose row 3 shows terra 0.121 s against PUC Lua 1.341 s; not A because the CPU is given only as 'AMD A10 3.8 GHz' and the Terra and Lua build flags are not stated.

corrections.workload: Scriptorium: recursive Fibonacci fib(34), whole-process wall time per run (bench.cc times system() calls, averaged over 5 runs, table keeps the best run), seconds, lower is better; 50 scripting-language implementations.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Compiled on VS2015 RC if possible, VS2013 elsewhere (per page); Terra build flags and version not stated (run.bat runs terra\terra tests\fib.t).
corrections.caveats: Single micro-benchmark (recursive fib(34)), July 2015, Windows 7; the page says 'Take it with a grain of salt'. tests/fib.t is a statically typed 'terra fib(a : int) : int' function compiled to native code through LLVM, so this is compiled int code against the dynamically typed PUC Lua interpreter; times include process startup and LLVM JIT compilation. LuaJIT (0.111 s, the Lua that Terra itself embeds) and plain MSVC C (0.074 s) were faster. Terra's LLVM dependency breaks the page's own 'no LLVM backends' rule. Terra version used is not stated (linked as zdevito/terra). Peer-reviewed Terra paper (PLDI 2013) was not reachable here. Scriptorium repo is archived (r-lyeh-archived, last commit 2016-05-24).

notes: Numbers match Scriptorium row 3 exactly (11.0x vs PUC Lua); tier B kept. Shortcomings: one recursive-fib test, typed LLVM-compiled code vs Lua interpreter, slower than LuaJIT on the same page, heavy LLVM dependency.

tier_reason: Independent third-party CI shootout (ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark, v8-v7 suite code in its v8-v7/ directory, results 10/5/2026) shows v8 Score 48107/64220/46932 vs QuickJS 1217/1761/1067 on ubuntu/macos-arm64/windows, and plb2 (CC0 code in src/, Apple M1) shows Node 21.5.0 well ahead of QuickJS; not A because the CI runners' CPU models and the prebuilt engines' compilers and flags are not stated.

corrections.caveats: Third-party shootout run by CI on GitHub-hosted runners; CPU model, compiler and flags are not stated and the engine binaries come from prebuilt per-engine build repos (ahaoboy/v8-build, ahaoboy/quickjs-build), so this is tier B rather than A. Versions on the page: v8 15.7.0 (ubuntu) and 15.7.35 (macos-arm64, windows), QuickJS 2026.06.04. The suite is an Octane/v8-v7 subset (Richards, DeltaBlue, Crypto, RayTrace, EarleyBoyer, RegExp, Splay, NavierStokes, forked from mozilla/arewefastyet) scored over a fixed time budget. V8 is top on ubuntu and windows but second to JavaScriptCore (67664) on macos-arm64. JIT engine vs interpreter-only baseline: V8 costs 28.8-66 MB on disk vs about 1 MB for QuickJS (Score/MB on ubuntu 729 vs 1190), so the comparison trades footprint for peak speed. The benchmark repo is small (59 stars). GitHub repo is a mirror of chromium.googlesource.com. plb2 numbers are from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/attractivechaos/plb2/HEAD/README.md (Node and Bun, not a bare V8 shell).

notes: All suite scores and plb2 times match the pages; derived ratios (about 40x, 36x, 44x) are correct. Shortcomings: CI runners without CPU model, prebuilt binaries with unknown flags, large footprint vs QuickJS, behind JavaScriptCore on macos-arm64.
